claims.text: The starting material is a green compact of refractory HEA elemental powders and TiH2 or ZrH2 containing 500–1000 ppm oxygen.
The required thermal history is 50°C/min to 600°C, a 2-hour hold, 10°C/min to 850°C, and a 4-hour hold at 850°C.
Processing under 2 GPa uniaxial pressure in vacuum with a hydrogen partial pressure of 10^-2 Pa is required.
Rapid heating to 600°C triggers exothermic decomposition of the Group IV hydrides and releases hydrogen gas.
Hydride decomposition maintains a transient hydrogen-rich reducing atmosphere during the critical decomposition window.
The released hydrogen scavenges surface oxygen and prevents stable oxide nuclei from forming.
The local hydrogen atmosphere kinetically inhibits oxygen diffusion into the metal lattice.
A pressure of 2 GPa suppresses void formation and promotes densification.
High-pressure extrusion at 850°C promotes solid-state diffusion and dynamic recrystallization of the BCC phase.
The proposed process prevents oxygen from nucleating brittle alpha-HCP phases.
The process traps the alloy as a metastable, oxygen-poor, single-phase BCC solid solution.
The resulting bulk material will exceed 99% of theoretical density.
The resulting material will have a ductile-to-brittle transition temperature below room temperature.
The resulting material will have a yield strength above 300 MPa at 1000°C.
Standard powder processing can introduce oxygen into a Nb-Mo-Ta-W-V-Ti refractory HEA during preparation.
Standard sintering in argon or vacuum typically causes alpha-HCP precipitation and brittle fracture at the transition temperature.
The proposed method applies specifically to refractory HEAs containing more than 15 at.% Group IV elements.
The method fails when the initial oxygen content exceeds 2000 ppm.
The method fails above an extrusion temperature of 1100°C.
Oxide stability increases significantly above 1100°C in the proposed alloy systems.

contradictions.description: The intervention specifies a vacuum environment below 10^-4 Pa, while the conditions specify an H2 partial pressure of 10^-2 Pa. These are incompatible if the former denotes total operating pressure rather than base pressure before backfilling.

The predicted transition temperature is merely below room temperature, but the hypothesis is declared falsified if it is above -50°C. A transition temperature between -50°C and room temperature would therefore satisfy the prediction while also triggering falsification.
The structural mediator states that the method avoids high-temperature exposure that would accelerate oxidation, whereas the prescribed history includes a four-hour hold at 850°C.
